_about: Predii-authored metadata for labor-guide rows. Each entry is matched to an XML row by component + note (exact text). id/row/name are WrenchIQ display fields; strong/kw are symptom keywords for ranking; parts feed the NAPA lookup; talk is the customer talk track for COMBINATION rows (kind: required | recommended | if-needed | optional; standalone: id of the same job done on its own).

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE AXLE SHAFT BOOT - Each Side
rows.name: Axle shaft boot, replace (each side)

talk.why: A torn boot lets dirt in and grease out, and that wears out the joint.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE AXLE SHAFT BOOT - Inner &/or Outer, Each Side
rows.name: Axle shaft boot, replace (inner and/or outer, each side)

talk.plain: replace the inner or outer CV axle boot
talk.why: A torn boot lets dirt in and grease out, and that wears out the joint.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE AXLE SHAFT CENTER SUPPORT BEARING
rows.name: Axle shaft center support bearing, replace

talk.plain: replace the axle's center support bearing
talk.why: It holds the long axle steady; a worn one causes a vibration at highway speed.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE CONSTANT VELOCITY JOINT - Each
rows.name: CV (constant velocity) joint, replace (each)

talk.why: A worn joint clicks when turning and can eventually let go.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE TRANSAXLE OUTPUT SEAL - Each
rows.name: Transaxle output seal, replace (each)

talk.plain: put in a new transmission output seal
talk.why: The seal gets disturbed when the axle comes out, and a new one prevents a fluid leak later.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REPLACE AXLE SHAFT - Each
rows.name: Axle shaft, replace (each)

talk.why: If the shaft is bent or its splines are worn, it is replaced while the assembly is already out.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REPLACE AXLE SHAFT - Each Side
rows.name: Axle shaft, replace (each side)

talk.why: If the shaft is bent or its splines are worn, it is replaced while the assembly is already out.

rows.note: COMBINATION - ADJUSTMENT PARKING BRAKE
rows.name: Parking brake, adjustment

talk.why: New brake parts change how the parking brake sits, so we set it to hold properly.

rows.note: COMBINATION - BLEED BRAKE SYSTEM - ABS Automated Bleed
rows.name: Brake system, bleed (ABS automated bleed)

talk.plain: bleed the brakes with the ABS scan tool
talk.why: If air gets into the ABS unit, this is the only way to get a firm pedal back.

rows.note: COMBINATION - BLEED BRAKE SYSTEM - Hydraulic Bleed
rows.name: Brake system, bleed (hydraulic bleed)

talk.why: Opening the brake system lets air in, and bleeding it keeps the pedal firm and safe.

rows.note: COMBINATION - BURNISH BRAKE ROTORS WHILE DRIVING VEHICLE DISC ROTOR
rows.name: Brake rotors, burnish while driving (disc rotor)

talk.plain: bed in the new brakes on a road test
talk.why: It seats the new pads to the rotors so they stop smoothly and quietly from day one.

rows.note: COMBINATION - BURNISH BRAKE ROTORS WHILE DRIVING VEHICLE DISC ROTOR
rows.name: Brake rotors, burnish while driving (disc rotor)

talk.plain: bed in the new brakes on a road test
talk.why: It seats the new pads to the rotors so they stop smoothly and quietly from day one.

rows.note: COMBINATION - CLEAN AND INSPECT HUB & ROTOR DISC -  Corrosion, Each - Clean any rust or corrosion from mating surface of Hub/Axle Flange and Brake Rotor.
rows.name: Hub & rotor disc, clean and inspect (corrosion, each)

talk.plain: clean the rust off the hub where the rotor sits
talk.why: Rust there makes the rotor wobble, which you feel as a pulsing pedal.

rows.note: COMBINATION - CLEAN AND INSPECT HUB & ROTOR DISC -  Corrosion, Each - Clean any rust or corrosion from mating surface of Hub/Axle Flange and Brake Rotor.
rows.name: Hub & rotor disc, clean and inspect (corrosion, each)

talk.plain: clean the rust off the hub where the rotor sits
talk.why: Rust there makes the rotor wobble, which you feel as a pulsing pedal.

rows.note: COMBINATION - CORRECT DISC ROTOR -  Lateral Runout, Each - Correct Rotor lateral runout by indexing.
rows.name: Disc rotor, correct lateral runout (each, by indexing)

talk.plain: correct rotor wobble by re-indexing it on the hub
talk.why: If the technician measures wobble, this fixes it without buying new parts.

rows.note: COMBINATION - CORRECT DISC ROTOR -  Lateral Runout, Each - Correct Rotor lateral runout by indexing.
rows.name: Disc rotor, correct lateral runout (each, by indexing)

talk.plain: correct rotor wobble by re-indexing it on the hub
talk.why: If the technician measures wobble, this fixes it without buying new parts.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REPLACE BRAKE HOSE - Each
rows.name: Brake hose, replace (each)

talk.why: Hoses crack with age, and the system is already open, so this is the cheapest time to do it.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REPLACE PARKING BRAKE SHOE & LINING - Each Side
rows.name: Parking brake shoe & lining, replace (each side)
parts: Parking brake shoe and lining kit

talk.why: Worn shoes mean the parking brake may not hold on a hill.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REPLACE WHEEL BEARING - FWD - Rear, Hub Assembly, One Side
rows.name: Wheel bearing, replace (FWD rear, hub assembly, one side)

talk.why: A worn bearing hums or growls and gets louder over time.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REPLACE WHEEL BEARING - FWD Front, One Side - DOES NOT include wheel alignment.
rows.name: Wheel bearing, replace (FWD front, one side) — does not include wheel alignment

talk.why: A worn bearing hums or growls and gets louder over time.

rows.note: COMBINATION - TESTING ANTI-LOCK BRAKE SYSTEM
rows.name: Anti-lock brake system, testing

talk.why: If the ABS light is on or a sensor was disturbed, this confirms the system works.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE DISC BRAKE PADS - Front, Both
rows.name: Front disc brake pads, replace (both sides)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE DISC BRAKE PADS - Rear, Both
rows.name: Rear disc brake pads, replace (both sides)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE DISC BRAKE PADS - Front & Rear
rows.name: Disc brake pads, replace (front and rear)

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE DISC BRAKE ROTOR - Each
rows.name: Disc brake rotor, replace with pads (each)

talk.why: If the rotor is worn below its minimum thickness, new pads on it will not stop well or last.

rows.note: COMBINATION - RESURFACE DISC BRAKE ROTOR - Each - Rotor removed from vehicle.
rows.name: Disc brake rotor, resurface (each)

talk.why: A smooth, flat rotor lets the new pads stop evenly without noise or pulsing.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REPLACE BRAKE PAD HARDWARE KIT - Each Axle
rows.name: Brake pad hardware kit, replace (each axle)

talk.plain: put in new pad clips and hardware
talk.why: Old clips rust and let the pads rattle or squeal, even when the pads are new.

rows.note: COMBINATION - BURNISH BRAKE ROTORS WHILE DRIVING VEHICLE DISC ROTOR
rows.name: Brake rotors, burnish while driving (disc rotor)

talk.plain: bed in the new brakes on a road test
talk.why: It seats the new pads to the rotors so they stop smoothly and quietly from day one.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE DISC BRAKE ROTOR - Front, Both - Includes R&I brake pads.
rows.name: Front disc brake rotors, replace (both sides)

rows.name: Front disc brake rotor, replace (one side)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE DISC BRAKE ROTOR - Rear, One Side - Includes R&I brake pads.
rows.name: Rear disc brake rotor, replace (one side)

rows.note: COMBINATION - CORRECT DISC ROTOR -  Lateral Runout, Each - Correct Rotor lateral runout by indexing.
rows.name: Disc rotor, correct lateral runout (each, by indexing)

talk.plain: correct rotor wobble by re-indexing it on the hub
talk.why: If the technician measures wobble, this fixes it without buying new parts.

rows.note: COMBINATION - CLEAN AND INSPECT HUB & ROTOR DISC -  Corrosion, Each
rows.name: Hub & rotor disc, clean and inspect (corrosion, each)

talk.plain: clean the rust off the hub where the rotor sits
talk.why: Rust there makes a new rotor wobble, which you feel as a pulsing pedal.

rows.name: Brake master cylinder, replace (includes bleed)

rows.note: COMBINATION - BLEED BRAKE SYSTEM - ABS Automated Bleed
rows.name: Brake system, bleed (ABS automated bleed)

talk.plain: bleed the brakes with the ABS scan tool
talk.why: If air gets into the ABS unit, this is the only way to get a firm pedal back.

rows.name: Brake fluid, flush (all wheels)

rows.name: Brake hose, replace (front, one side, includes bleed)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE BRAKE HOSE - Rear, One Side - Includes bleed system.
rows.name: Brake hose, replace (rear, one side, includes bleed)

rows.name: Wheel speed sensor, replace (front, one side)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE WHEEL SPEED SENSOR - Rear, One Side
rows.name: Wheel speed sensor, replace (rear, one side)

rows.note: COMBINATION - TESTING ANTI-LOCK BRAKE SYSTEM
rows.name: Anti-lock brake system, testing

talk.why: It confirms the new sensor reads correctly and the ABS light stays off.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE PARKING BRAKE CABLE - Rear, One Side
rows.name: Parking brake cable, replace (rear, one side)

rows.note: COMBINATION - ADJUSTMENT PARKING BRAKE
rows.name: Parking brake, adjustment

talk.why: A new cable has to be set to the right tension or the parking brake will not hold.

rows.name: A/C system, performance and pressure test

rows.name: A/C compressor, replace (recharge extra)

rows.note: COMBINATION - EVACUATE & RECHARGE A/C SYSTEM
rows.name: A/C system, evacuate and recharge (with compressor)

talk.why: Any time the A/C system is opened it has to be vacuumed out and refilled to the exact amount, or it will not cool.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE RECEIVER DRIER / DESICCANT
rows.name: A/C receiver drier / desiccant, replace

talk.why: It traps moisture, and most compressor warranties require a new one with a new compressor.

rows.note: COMBINATION - FLUSH A/C SYSTEM
rows.name: A/C system, flush

talk.why: If the old compressor shed metal, flushing keeps that debris from killing the new one.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE A/C COMPRESSOR CLUTCH - Compressor on vehicle
rows.name: A/C compressor clutch, replace (compressor on vehicle)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE A/C CONDENSER - DOES NOT include evacuate & recharge.
rows.name: A/C condenser, replace (recharge extra)

rows.note: COMBINATION - EVACUATE & RECHARGE A/C SYSTEM
rows.name: A/C system, evacuate and recharge (with condenser)

talk.why: Any time the A/C system is opened it has to be vacuumed out and refilled to the exact amount, or it will not cool.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE RECEIVER DRIER / DESICCANT
rows.name: A/C receiver drier / desiccant, replace (with condenser)

talk.why: It traps moisture, and once the system is open the old one is used up.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE EVAPORATOR CORE - Front - Includes R&I instrument panel. DOES NOT include evacuate & recharge.
rows.name: A/C evaporator core, replace (front, dash removal; recharge extra)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE EVAPORATOR CORE - Rear - DOES NOT include evacuate & recharge.
rows.name: A/C evaporator core, replace (rear; recharge extra)

rows.note: COMBINATION - EVACUATE & RECHARGE A/C SYSTEM
rows.name: A/C system, evacuate and recharge (with evaporator)

talk.why: Any time the A/C system is opened it has to be vacuumed out and refilled to the exact amount, or it will not cool.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE EXPANSION VALVE - Each
rows.name: A/C expansion valve, replace with evaporator (each)

talk.why: It bolts to the evaporator, so it is right there, and an old valve is a common cause of poor cooling.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE HEATER CORE - Front
rows.name: Heater core, replace with front evaporator

talk.why: It sits next to the evaporator behind the dash; doing it now avoids taking the dash apart a second time.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE EXPANSION VALVE - Front - DOES NOT include evacuate & recharge.
rows.name: A/C expansion valve, replace (front; recharge extra)

rows.note: COMBINATION - EVACUATE & RECHARGE A/C SYSTEM
rows.name: A/C system, evacuate and recharge (with expansion valve)

talk.why: Any time the A/C system is opened it has to be vacuumed out and refilled to the exact amount, or it will not cool.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE A/C PRESSURE SENSOR - DOES NOT include evacuate & recharge.
rows.name: A/C pressure sensor, replace (recharge extra)

rows.note: COMBINATION - EVACUATE & RECHARGE A/C SYSTEM
rows.name: A/C system, evacuate and recharge (with pressure sensor)

talk.why: Any time the A/C system is opened it has to be vacuumed out and refilled to the exact amount, or it will not cool.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE BLOWER MOTOR - Rear
rows.name: Blower motor, replace (rear)

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE BLOWER MOTOR RESISTOR - Front
rows.name: Blower motor resistor, replace with blower motor

talk.why: A failing motor often burns out the resistor, and it is right next to it.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE BLOWER MOTOR RESISTOR - Front
rows.name: Blower motor resistor, replace (front)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE HEATER CORE - Front - Includes R&I instrument panel and drain & refill coolant.
rows.name: Heater core, replace (front, dash removal)

rows.name: Cabin air filter, replace

rows.name: Water pump, replace (includes coolant drain and refill)

rows.name: Drive belt, replace with water pump

talk.plain: put on a new drive belt
talk.why: The belt comes off for this job anyway, and an old one is the next thing to squeal or break.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE THERMOSTAT
rows.name: Thermostat, replace with water pump

talk.why: The coolant is already drained, and an old thermostat is a common cause of overheating later.

rows.note: COMBINATION - FLUSH COOLING SYSTEM
rows.name: Cooling system, flush with water pump

talk.why: It clears old deposits so the new pump is not circulating dirty coolant.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE THERMOSTAT - Includes drain & refill coolant.
rows.name: Thermostat, replace (includes coolant drain and refill)

rows.note: COMBINATION - FLUSH COOLING SYSTEM
rows.name: Cooling system, flush with thermostat

talk.why: It clears old deposits so the new thermostat is not sitting in dirty coolant.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE RADIATOR - Includes drain & refill coolant.
rows.name: Radiator, replace (includes coolant drain and refill)

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE RADIATOR HOSE - Upper
rows.name: Upper radiator hose, replace with radiator

talk.why: It comes off with the radiator, and a soft or cracked hose is the next leak.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE RADIATOR HOSE - Lower
rows.name: Lower radiator hose, replace with radiator

talk.why: It comes off with the radiator, and a soft or cracked hose is the next leak.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE THERMOSTAT
rows.name: Thermostat, replace with radiator

talk.why: The coolant is already drained, and an old thermostat is a common cause of overheating later.

rows.note: COMBINATION - FLUSH COOLING SYSTEM
rows.name: Cooling system, flush with radiator

talk.why: It clears old deposits so they do not clog the new radiator.

rows.name: Upper radiator hose, replace (includes coolant drain and refill)

rows.name: Battery, replace

rows.name: Battery terminals and cables, clean

talk.plain: clean the battery terminals and cables
talk.why: Corrosion on the cables can make a brand-new battery act like a weak one.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE ALTERNATOR
rows.name: Alternator, replace

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE DRIVE BELT
rows.name: Drive belt, replace with alternator

talk.plain: put on a new drive belt
talk.why: The belt comes off for this job anyway, and a worn belt can slip and undercharge the new alternator.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE DRIVE BELT TENSIONER
rows.name: Drive belt tensioner, replace with alternator

talk.why: A weak tensioner lets the belt slip, and it is right there with the belt off.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE STARTER MOTOR - Includes R&I intake plenum.
rows.name: Starter motor, replace (includes intake plenum R&I)

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE INTAKE PLENUM GASKET
rows.name: Intake plenum gasket, replace with starter

talk.plain: put in a new intake plenum gasket
talk.why: The intake comes off to reach the starter, and the old gasket cannot be reused without risking a vacuum leak.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE DRIVE BELT
rows.name: Drive belt, replace

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE DRIVE BELT TENSIONER - Includes R&I drive belt.
rows.name: Drive belt tensioner, replace

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE IDLER PULLEY - Each
rows.name: Idler pulley, replace with tensioner (each)

talk.why: A worn pulley bearing makes the same squeal or chirp as a bad tensioner.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE SPARK PLUGS - All - Includes R&I intake plenum.
rows.name: Spark plugs, replace all (includes intake plenum R&I)

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE IGNITION COIL - Each
rows.name: Ignition coil, replace with spark plugs (each)

talk.why: If a coil tests weak, swapping it now avoids taking the intake apart again for a misfire.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE IGNITION COIL - Front Bank, One
rows.name: Ignition coil, replace (front bank, one)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE IGNITION COIL - Rear Bank, One - Includes R&I intake plenum.
rows.name: Ignition coil, replace (rear bank, one; includes intake plenum R&I)

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE IGNITION COIL - Each Additional, Same Bank
rows.name: Ignition coil, replace each additional (same bank)

talk.plain: replace another coil on the same side
talk.why: Coils of the same age tend to fail one after another.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE SPARK PLUG - Each
rows.name: Spark plug, replace with coil (each)

talk.plain: replace the spark plug under that coil
talk.why: A worn plug is often what overworked the coil, and it is right under it.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE VALVE COVER GASKET - Front Bank
rows.name: Valve cover gasket, replace (front bank)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE VALVE COVER GASKET - Rear Bank - Includes R&I intake plenum.
rows.name: Valve cover gasket, replace (rear bank; includes intake plenum R&I)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE VALVE COVER GASKET - Both
rows.name: Valve cover gaskets, replace (both banks)

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE SPARK PLUGS - All
rows.name: Spark plugs, replace all with valve cover gaskets

talk.why: The plugs sit under the valve covers, so the access labor is already done.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE AIR/FUEL RATIO SENSOR - Upstream, Bank 1
rows.name: Air/fuel ratio sensor, replace (upstream, bank 1)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE AIR/FUEL RATIO SENSOR - Upstream, Bank 2
rows.name: Air/fuel ratio sensor, replace (upstream, bank 2)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE OXYGEN SENSOR - Downstream, Each
rows.name: Oxygen sensor, replace (downstream, each)

rows.note: CLEAN THROTTLE BODY - Includes idle relearn.
rows.name: Throttle body, clean (includes idle relearn)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE THROTTLE BODY - Includes idle relearn.
rows.name: Throttle body, replace (includes idle relearn)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE MASS AIR FLOW SENSOR
rows.name: Mass air flow sensor, replace

rows.note: DIAGNOSE CHECK ENGINE LIGHT - Includes scan & code interpretation.
rows.name: Diagnostic: check engine light (scan and interpret codes)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE STRUT ASSEMBLY - Front, One Side - DOES NOT include wheel alignment.
rows.name: Front strut assembly, replace (one side; alignment extra)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE STRUT ASSEMBLY - Front, Both - DOES NOT include wheel alignment.
rows.name: Front strut assemblies, replace (both sides; alignment extra)

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE STRUT MOUNT & BEARING - Each
rows.name: Strut mount and bearing, replace with strut (each)

talk.plain: replace the strut mount and bearing
talk.why: An old mount can clunk or make the steering feel notchy, even with a new strut.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE COIL SPRING - Each
rows.name: Coil spring, replace with strut (each)

talk.why: A cracked or sagging spring changes ride height and wears the new strut faster.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE STABILIZER BAR LINK - Each
rows.name: Stabilizer bar link, replace with strut (each)

talk.why: It bolts to the strut, and a worn link is a common source of clunks over bumps.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE SHOCK ABSORBER - Rear, One Side
rows.name: Rear shock absorber, replace (one side)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE SHOCK ABSORBER - Rear, Both
rows.name: Rear shock absorbers, replace (both sides)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE STABILIZER BAR LINK - Front, One Side
rows.name: Front stabilizer bar link, replace (one side)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE STABILIZER BAR LINK - Front, Both
rows.name: Front stabilizer bar links, replace (both sides)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE LOWER CONTROL ARM - Front, One Side - DOES NOT include wheel alignment.
rows.name: Front lower control arm, replace (one side; alignment extra)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE LOWER CONTROL ARM - Front, Both - DOES NOT include wheel alignment.
rows.name: Front lower control arms, replace (both sides; alignment extra)

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE LOWER BALL JOINT - Each
rows.name: Lower ball joint, replace with control arm (each)

talk.why: A loose ball joint is a safety item, and the arm is already off.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE CONTROL ARM BUSHING - Each
rows.name: Control arm bushing, replace (each)

talk.why: Cracked bushings cause clunks and uneven tire wear.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE OUTER TIE ROD END - One Side - DOES NOT include wheel alignment.
rows.name: Outer tie rod end, replace (one side; alignment extra)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE OUTER TIE ROD END - Both - DOES NOT include wheel alignment.
rows.name: Outer tie rod ends, replace (both sides; alignment extra)

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE INNER TIE ROD - Each
rows.name: Inner tie rod, replace with outer (each)

talk.why: If the inner joint is loose too, the steering stays sloppy with only the outer replaced.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE STEERING RACK BOOT - Each
rows.name: Steering rack boot, replace (each)

talk.why: A torn boot lets water into the steering rack, which is a much bigger repair.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE WHEEL BEARING & HUB - Front, One Side - DOES NOT include wheel alignment.
rows.name: Front wheel bearing and hub, replace (one side)

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE WHEEL BEARING & HUB - Rear, One Side
rows.name: Rear wheel bearing and hub, replace (one side)

rows.note: CHECK WHEEL ALIGNMENT
rows.name: Wheel alignment, check

rows.note: WHEEL ALIGNMENT - Four Wheel - Includes check & adjust.
rows.name: Wheel alignment, four wheel (check and adjust)

rows.note: ROTATE TIRES - Four Wheel
rows.name: Tires, rotate (four wheel)

rows.note: MOUNT & BALANCE TIRES - Four Wheel
rows.name: Tires, mount and balance (four wheel)

rows.note: BALANCE TIRES - Four Wheel
rows.name: Tires, balance (four wheel)

rows.note: REPAIR TIRE - Flat, Each - Plug & patch.
rows.name: Tire, repair flat (plug and patch, each)

rows.note: COMBINATION - BALANCE TIRES - Four Wheel
rows.name: Tires, balance with rotation (four wheel)

talk.why: The wheels are already off for the rotation, and balancing smooths out highway vibration.

rows.note: COMBINATION - REMOVE & REPLACE TIRE PRESSURE SENSOR - Each - Tire dismounted.
rows.name: Tire pressure sensor, replace with tire off (each)

talk.why: Sensor batteries die with age; with the tire already off it is a fraction of the labor.

rows.note: REMOVE & REPLACE TIRE PRESSURE SENSOR - Each - Includes dismount, mount, balance and relearn.
rows.name: Tire pressure sensor, replace (each, includes relearn)
